claims.text: Laser cladding can produce an in situ graded interfacial alloy layer between preformed tungsten regions and a copper matrix.
The graded laser-cladded W–Cu interface will eliminate interfacial voids.
The graded laser-cladded W–Cu interface will eliminate phase separation.
The intervention will preserve mechanical durability under fusion-reactor conditions.
Conventionally produced or metal-3D-printed W–Cu composites typically have interface voids and phase separation.
Controlled laser energy density will locally melt and alloy the W–Cu interface.
Laser cladding of the W–Cu interface will form a transient liquid phase that rapidly solidifies into a graded interlayer.
Temperatures up to approximately 1200 °C are representative of fusion-reactor first-wall service conditions for the proposed joint.
The resulting interface will transition smoothly in composition from pure tungsten to copper.
The graded interfacial composition will enhance atomic diffusion and interfacial bonding.
Laser cladding induces transient liquid-phase sintering at the W–Cu interface.
Transient liquid-phase sintering promotes W–Cu atomic interdiffusion and eliminates microvoids.
The graded bonding layer reduces interfacial thermal resistance and mitigates phase separation.
Reduced thermal resistance and phase separation enhance thermal transport and mechanical durability at high temperature and under irradiation.
Relative to metal 3D printing or spark-plasma sintering, laser-cladded W–Cu will have lower interfacial void density and a more uniform junction.
Relative to the named baseline, laser-cladded W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity.
Relative to the named baseline, laser-cladded W–Cu will retain mechanical properties better during high-temperature annealing and irradiation.
Metal 3D printing and spark-plasma sintering baselines suffer from phase separation, void formation, and limited W–Cu interfacial bonding.
Prolonged or cyclic irradiation may degrade the laser-cladded graded interlayer.
Transient liquid-phase formation may introduce phases that impair long-term performance.
